title: ftypes + dfilter: Switch FT_EUI64 underlying type to bytes
description:
Switch the underlying type of FT_EUI64 to bytes, similar to other
network addresses. This allows slicing into bytes to work, e.g.
filters like "wpan.src64[:3] == eth.src[:3]" for Zigbee Encapsulation
Protocol. This matches the treatment in the address type AT_EUI64.

Note that the existing raw bytes addressing with @ has different
results, as IEEE 802.15.4 requires that EUI-64 addresses (and all
other address fields) are transmitted from the right most octet to
the left most octet, i.e. in Little Endian byte order. (See
IEEE 802.15.4-202 4.5 Transmission order.)  Thus @wpan.src64[0]
(before or after this change) refers to the first byte transmitted,
the RMO, which is the last byte when presented as a byte string.

This makes FT_EUI64 compatible with the other address field types
(except for FT_IPXNET) and FT_BYTES, and no longer compatible with
the integer types. Slicing, comparing with bytes types, and registering
multiple address fields that are FT_ETHER and FT_EUI64 to the same
abbreviation is allowed. Integer arithmetic is no longer allowed on
FT_EUI64 (as with other bytes types.) Continue to allow FT_EUI64
to be specified in the packet matching language with 64 bit unsigned
integer literals, though.

API calls like proto_tree_add_eui64 still take a 64-bit unsigned
integer in host byte order, which does have an advantage of preventing
any issues with a short length.
